The most powerful refutation is the “pleasure machine”/experience-machine objection (and its utilitarian cousin, the “utility monster”): it shows that summing intensities and durations of pleasure cannot capture what makes lives go well, since we would not accept endless simulated bliss or sacrificing one person’s一切 to a monster’s greater total. This defeats the calculus by proving its core metric is the wrong currency for value, not merely hard to measure.  
CONFIDENCE: 82
